title.zh: 卷一百〇二 表第三 諸王世表三
title.raw: 卷一百〇二 表第三 諸王世表三 Volume 102 Tables 3: Princes 3

sentences.zh: 慶 靖王㮵，太祖庶十六子，二十四年封。二十六年就藩韋州。建文三年遷寧夏。正統三年薨。

translations.literal: Qing: Prince Jing, the sixteenth son by a concubine of Taizu, was enfeoffed in the twenty-fourth year. In the twenty-sixth year he went to his fief at Weizhou. In the third year of Jianwen he was moved to Ningxia. He died in the third year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: Qing princedom — Prince Jing, Taizu's sixteenth son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in Hongwu year 24, took up his fief at Weizhou in year 26, was transferred to Ningxia in Jianwen year 3, and died in Zhengtong year 3.

sentences.zh: 康王秩煃，靖庶一子，正統四年襲封。成化五年薨。

translations.literal: King Kang Rank Huang, the first son by a concubine of Prince Jing, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the fourth year of Zhengtong. He died in the fifth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: King Kang (Rank Huang), Prince Jing's first son by a concubine, inherited the title in Zhengtong year 4 and died in Chenghua year 5.

sentences.zh: 懷王邃𡓱，康庶一子，初封平原王，成化七年襲封。十五年薨。無子。 莊王邃塀，康庶二子，初封岐陽王，成化十七年進封。弘治四年薨。

translations.literal: King Huai Sui 𡓱, the first son by a concubine of King Kang, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyuan, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the seventh year of Chenghua, and died in the fifteenth year. He had no sons. King Zhuang Sui Bing, the second son by a concubine of King Kang, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Qiyang, advanced to enfeoffment in the seventeenth year of Chenghua, and died in the fourth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: King Huai (Sui 𡓱), King Kang's first son by a concubine, was first made Prince of Pingyuan, succeeded in Chenghua year 7, and died in year 15 without heirs. King Zhuang (Sui Bing), King Kang's second son by a concubine, was first made Prince of Qiyang, was promoted to the main line in Chenghua year 17, and died in Hongzhi year 4.

sentences.zh: 恭王寘錖，莊庶一子，初封落交王，弘治七年襲封。十一年薨。

translations.literal: King Gong Zhi Qian, the first son by a concubine of King Zhuang, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Luojiao, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the seventh year of Hongzhi, and died in the eleventh year.
translations.idiomatic: King Gong (Zhi Qian), King Zhuang's first son by a concubine, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Luojiao, inherited the title in Hongzhi year 7, and died in year 11.

sentences.zh: 台浤，恭庶一子，弘治十六年襲封。後革為庶人。嘉靖三十年卒。以二子鼒枋襲封。追復王，諡曰定。

translations.literal: Tai Hong, the first son by a concubine of King Gong, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the sixteenth year of Hongzhi. Later he was reduced to commoner status. He died in the thirtieth year of Jiajing. His two sons Zi Fang succeeded to the enfeoffment. He was posthumously restored as king, with the posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Hong, King Gong's first son by a concubine, inherited in Hongzhi year 16 but was later stripped to commoner rank. He died in Jiajing year 30; succession passed through his two sons Zi Fang, and he was posthumously restored as king with the posthumous epithet Ding.

sentences.zh: 鼒櫍，定庶一子，封世子。薨，諡端和。 惠王鼒枋，定庶二子，嘉靖二十年以桐鄉王改封世子。三十一年襲封。萬曆二年薨。

translations.literal: Zi Chi, the first son by a concubine of King Ding, was enfeoffed as heir apparent. He died; his posthumous title was Duanhe. King Hui Zi Fang, the second son by a concubine of King Ding, in the twentieth year of Jiajing was changed from Prince of Tongxiang to heir apparent enfeoffment. He succeeded in the thirty-first year and died in the second year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Chi, King Ding's first son by a concubine, was made heir apparent and died with the posthumous title Duanhe. King Hui (Zi Fang), King Ding's second son by a concubine, was transferred from Prince of Tongxiang to heir apparent in Jiajing year 20, succeeded in year 31, and died in Wanli year 2.

sentences.zh: 端王倪𤏳，惠嫡一子，嘉靖三十七年封世子。萬曆五年襲封。十六年薨。

translations.literal: King Duan Ni 𤏳, the first son by the principal wife of King Hui, was enfeoffed as heir apparent in the thirty-seventh year of Jiajing. He succeeded in the fifth year of Wanli and died in the sixteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: King Duan (Ni 𤏳), King Hui's eldest son by his principal consort, was made heir apparent in Jiajing year 37, inherited in Wanli year 5, and died in year 16.

sentences.zh: 憲王伸域，端庶一子，初封綏德王，萬曆十九年襲封，本年薨。

translations.literal: King Xian Shen Yu, the first son by a concubine of King Duan, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Suide. He succeeded in the nineteenth year of Wanli and died in the same year.
translations.idiomatic: King Xian (Shen Yu), King Duan's first son by a concubine, was first Prince of Suide, inherited in Wanli year 19, and died that same year.

sentences.zh: 王帥鋅，憲嫡二子，萬曆二十三年襲封，薨。

translations.literal: Prince Shuai Xin, the second son by the principal wife of King Xian, succeeded in the twenty-third year of Wanli and died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shuai (Xin), King Xian's second son by his principal consort, inherited in Wanli year 23 and died.

sentences.zh: 王倬㴶，帥鋅嫡一子，萬曆四十五年封世子，既而襲封。

translations.literal: Prince Zhuo, the first son by the principal wife of Prince Shuai Xin, was enfeoffed as heir apparent in the forty-fifth year of Wanli and soon afterward succeeded to the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhuo, Prince Shuai Xin's eldest son by his principal consort, was made heir apparent in Wanli year 45 and soon succeeded to the title.

cells.content: 靖寧 王秩燾，靖庶二子，封後薨。無子，除。

translations.literal: Jingning: Prince Rank Tao, the second son by a concubine of Prince Jing, was enfeoffed and afterward died. He had no sons; the line was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Jingning — Prince Rank Tao, Prince Jing's second son by a concubine, received his enfeoffment and died without heirs; the line was abolished.

cells.translation: Jingning — Prince Rank Tao, Prince Jing's second son by a concubine, received his enfeoffment and died without heirs; the line was abolished.

cells.content: 真寧 莊惠王秩榮，靖庶三子，景泰六年封。成化三年薨。

translations.literal: Zhenning: King Zhuanghui Rank Rong, the third son by a concubine of Prince Jing, was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Jingtai and died in the third year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenning — King Zhuanghui (Rank Rong), Prince Jing's third son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in Jingtai year 6 and died in Chenghua year 3.

cells.content: 康簡王邃垿，莊惠庶一子，天順元年襲封。成化十二年薨。

translations.literal: King Kangjian Sui Xu, the first son by a concubine of King Zhuanghui, succeeded in the first year of Tianshun and died in the twelfth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: King Kangjian (Sui Xu), King Zhuanghui's first son by a concubine, inherited in Tianshun 1 and died in Chenghua year 12.

cells.content: 溫穆王寘䥵，康簡嫡一子，弘治三年襲封。十五年薨。

translations.literal: King Wenmu Zhi, the first son by the principal wife of King Kangjian, succeeded in the third year of Hongzhi and died in the fifteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: King Wenmu (Zhi ), King Kangjian's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Hongzhi year 3 and died in year 15.

cells.content: 榮僖王台涍，溫穆嫡一子，正德元年襲封。十年薨。

translations.literal: King Rongxi Tai Jiao, the first son by the principal wife of King Wenmu, succeeded in the first year of Zhengde and died in the tenth year.
translations.idiomatic: King Rongxi (Tai Jiao), King Wenmu's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Zhengde 1 and died in year 10.

cells.content: 安惠王鼒㮿，榮僖嫡一子，正德十六年襲封。嘉靖三十一年薨。

translations.literal: King Anhui Zi, the first son by the principal wife of King Rongxi, succeeded in the sixteenth year of Zhengde and died in the thirty-first year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: King Anhui (Zi ), King Rongxi's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Zhengde year 16 and died in Jiajing year 31.

translations.literal: King Gongjian Ni 𤇼, the first son by the principal wife of King Anhui, succeeded in the thirty-third year of Jiajing and died in the fifth year of Wanli. He had no sons; the line was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: King Gongjian (Ni 𤇼), King Anhui's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Jiajing year 33, died in Wanli year 5 without heirs, and the line was abolished.

cells.content: 安化 惠懿王秩炵，靖庶四子，永樂十九年封。弘治十五年薨。

translations.literal: Anhua: King Huiyi Rank Tong, the fourth son by a concubine of Prince Jing, was enfeoffed in the nineteenth year of Yongle and died in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Anhua — King Huiyi (Rank Tong), Prince Jing's fourth son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in Yongle year 19 and died in Hongzhi year 15.

cells.content: 邃墁，惠懿庶一子，初封鎮國將軍。天順八年卒。以子寘鐇襲封，追封王，諡恭和。

translations.literal: Sui Man, the first son by a concubine of King Huiyi, was first enfeoffed as Defender of the State General. He died in the eighth year of Tianshun. His son Zhi Zheng succeeded to the enfeoffment; he was posthumously enfeoffed as king with the posthumous title Gonghe.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Man, King Huiyi's first son by a concubine, was first made Defender of the State General and died in Tianshun year 8; his son Zhi Zheng inherited the line, and Sui Man was posthumously made king with the epithet Gonghe.

cells.content: 寘鐇，恭和庶一子，弘治五年襲封。正德五年叛逆伏誅，除。

translations.literal: Zhi Zheng, the first son by a concubine of King Gonghe, succeeded in the fifth year of Hongzhi. In the fifth year of Zhengde he rebelled and was executed; the line was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Zheng, King Gonghe's first son by a concubine, inherited in Hongzhi year 5, rebelled and was executed in Zhengde year 5, and the line was abolished.

cells.content: 岐山 悼莊王秩煉，靖庶五子，封後薨。無子，除。

translations.literal: Qishan: King Daozhuang Rank Lian, the fifth son by a concubine of Prince Jing, was enfeoffed and afterward died. He had no sons; the line was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Qishan — King Daozhuang (Rank Lian), Prince Jing's fifth son by a concubine, was enfeoffed and died without heirs; the line was abolished.

cells.content: 安塞 宣靖王秩炅，靖庶六子，正統九年封。成化九年薨。無子，除。

translations.literal: Ansei: King Xuanjing Rank Jiong, the sixth son by a concubine of Prince Jing, was enfeoffed in the ninth year of Zhengtong and died in the ninth year of Chenghua. He had no sons; the line was abolished.

cells.content: 弘農 安僖王邃㙉，康庶三子，天順三年封。弘治三年薨。

translations.literal: Hongnong: King Anxi Sui, the third son by a concubine of King Kang, was enfeoffed in the third year of Tianshun and died in the third year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Hongnong — King Anxi (Sui ), King Kang's third son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in Tianshun year 3 and died in Hongzhi year 3.

cells.content: 榮惠王寘鑭，安僖庶一子，弘治五年襲封。正德三年薨。

translations.literal: King Ronghui Zhi Lan, the first son by a concubine of King Anxi, succeeded in the fifth year of Hongzhi and died in the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: King Ronghui (Zhi Lan), King Anxi's first son by a concubine, inherited in Hongzhi year 5 and died in Zhengde year 3.

cells.content: 恭定王台泙，榮惠嫡一子，正德十年襲封。嘉靖二十八年薨。

translations.literal: King Gongding Tai Ping, the first son by the principal wife of King Ronghui, succeeded in the tenth year of Zhengde and died in the twenty-eighth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: King Gongding (Tai Ping), King Ronghui's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Zhengde year 10 and died in Jiajing year 28.

translations.idiomatic: King Kangxi (Zi 𰘆), King Gongding's first son by a concubine, inherited in Jiajing year 33 and died in Longqing year 6.

translations.literal: King Gongshun Ni Long, the first son by the principal wife of King Kangxi, was enfeoffed as eldest son in the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing. He succeeded in the third year of Wanli and died in the seventeenth year.
translations.idiomatic: King Gongshun (Ni Long), King Kangxi's eldest son by his principal consort, was made eldest son in Jiajing year 38, inherited in Wanli year 3, and died in year 17.

translations.literal: Prince Shen, the first son by the principal wife of King Gongshun, was enfeoffed as eldest son in the tenth year of Wanli. He succeeded in the twenty-first year and died.

cells.content: 豐林 溫僖王邃㙂，康庶六子，成化八年封。正德六年薨。

cells.content: 臨川 磐煇，獻庶二子，宣德元年封。天順五年，罪降庶人，鳳陽居住。成化二十一年卒。嘉靖三十五年追復王，諡康僖。

translations.literal: Linchuan: Pan Hui, the second son by a concubine of Prince Xian, was enfeoffed in the first year of Xuande. In the fifth year of Tianshun, for a crime he was reduced to commoner status and made to reside at Fengyang. He died in the twenty-first year of Chenghua. In the thirty-fifth year of Jiajing he was posthumously restored as king with the posthumous title Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Linchuan — Pan Hui, Prince Xian's second son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in Xuande 1; in Tianshun year 5 he was demoted to commoner rank for a crime and sent to live at Fengyang, died in Chenghua year 21, and was posthumously restored as king with the epithet Kangxi in Jiajing year 35.

cells.content: 奠埨，康僖嫡一子，正德七年封長子。天順五年，罪降庶人，守西山祖墳。成化八年卒。嘉靖二十五年追封王，諡恭順。子孫不襲，除。

translations.literal: Dian Jun, the first son by the principal wife of King Kangxi, was enfeoffed as eldest son in the seventh year of Zhengde. In the fifth year of Tianshun, for a crime he was reduced to commoner status and made to guard the ancestral tombs on West Mountain. He died in the eighth year of Chenghua. In the twenty-fifth year of Jiajing he was posthumously enfeoffed as king with the posthumous title Gongshun. His descendants did not succeed; the line was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Dian Jun, King Kangxi's eldest son by his principal consort, was made eldest son in Zhengde year 7; in Tianshun year 5 he was demoted to commoner rank for a crime and assigned to guard the West Mountain ancestral tombs, died in Chenghua year 8, was posthumously made king with the epithet Gongshun in Jiajing year 25, and his descendants did not inherit — the line was abolished.

cells.content: 宜春 安簡王磐烑，獻庶三子，宣德三年封。弘治五年薨。

translations.literal: Yichun: King Anjian Pan Yao, the third son by a concubine of Prince Xian, was enfeoffed in the third year of Xuande and died in the fifth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yichun — King Anjian (Pan Yao), Prince Xian's third son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in Xuande year 3 and died in Hongzhi year 5.

cells.content: 宣和王奠坫，安簡嫡一子，弘治八年襲封。九年薨。

translations.literal: King Xuanhe Dian Dian, the first son by the principal wife of King Anjian, succeeded in the eighth year of Hongzhi and died in the ninth year.
translations.idiomatic: King Xuanhe (Dian Dian), King Anjian's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Hongzhi year 8 and died in year 9.

cells.content: 覲鐏，宣和嫡一子，弘治八年封長子。九年卒。以子宸澮襲封。追封王，諡懷簡。

translations.literal: Guan Zun, the first son by the principal wife of King Xuanhe, was enfeoffed as eldest son in the eighth year of Hongzhi and died in the ninth year. His son Chen Huan succeeded to the enfeoffment; he was posthumously enfeoffed as king with the posthumous title Huaijian.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zun, King Xuanhe's eldest son by his principal consort, was made eldest son in Hongzhi year 8 and died in year 9; his son Chen Huan inherited the line, and Guan Zun was posthumously made king with the epithet Huaijian.

cells.content: 康僖王宸澮，懷簡嫡一子，弘治十一年襲封。十三年薨。

translations.literal: King Kangxi Chen Huan, the first son by the principal wife of King Huaijian, succeeded in the eleventh year of Hongzhi and died in the thirteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: King Kangxi (Chen Huan), King Huaijian's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Hongzhi year 11 and died in year 13.

cells.content: 拱樤，康僖嫡一子，正德二年襲封。十五年坐宸濠反，解京自盡，子送鳳陽，除。

translations.literal: Gong, the first son by the principal wife of King Kangxi, succeeded in the second year of Zhengde. In the fifteenth year, implicated in Chen Hao's rebellion, he was sent to the capital and compelled to take his own life; his sons were sent to Fengyang; the line was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Gong, King Kangxi's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Zhengde year 2; in year 15, implicated in Chen Hao's rebellion, he was brought to the capital and forced to commit suicide, his sons were sent to Fengyang, and the line was abolished.

cells.content: 新昌 安僖王磐炷，獻庶四子，宣德五年封。天順三年薨。無子，除。

translations.literal: Xinchang: King Anxi Pan Zhu, the fourth son by a concubine of Prince Xian, was enfeoffed in the fifth year of Xuande and died in the third year of Tianshun. He had no sons; the line was abolished.

cells.content: 信豐 悼惠王磐㷬，獻庶五子，宣德七年封。正德四年薨。無子，除。

translations.literal: Xinfeng: King Daohui Pan, the fifth son by a concubine of Prince Xian, was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Xuande and died in the fourth year of Zhengde. He had no sons; the line was abolished.

cells.content: 瑞昌 恭僖王奠墠，惠庶二子，景泰二年以鎮國將軍加封。成化十二年薨。

translations.literal: Ruichang: King Gongxi Dian Shan, the second son by a concubine of King Hui, in the second year of Jingtai received an additional enfeoffment as Defender of the State General. He died in the twelfth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: Ruichang — King Gongxi (Dian Shan), King Hui's second son by a concubine, was additionally enfeoffed from Defender of the State General rank in Jingtai year 2 and died in Chenghua year 12.

translations.literal: King Rong'an Guan Yi, the first son by the principal wife of King Gongxi, succeeded in the fourteenth year of Chenghua and died in the first year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: King Rong'an (Guan Yi), King Gongxi's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Chenghua year 14 and died in Hongzhi 1.

cells.content: 宸㵾，榮安庶一子，初封鎮國將軍。弘治三年卒。本年追封王，諡悼順。

translations.literal: Chen, the first son by a concubine of King Rong'an, was first enfeoffed as Defender of the State General. He died in the third year of Hongzhi. In the same year he was posthumously enfeoffed as king with the posthumous title Daoshun.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, King Rong'an's first son by a concubine, was first made Defender of the State General, died in Hongzhi year 3, and was posthumously made king that same year with the epithet Daoshun.

cells.content: 拱栟，悼順嫡一子，弘治十二年襲封。正德十五年坐宸濠反死，子送鳳陽，除。

translations.literal: Gong Bing, the first son by the principal wife of King Daoshun, succeeded in the twelfth year of Hongzhi. In the fifteenth year of Zhengde, implicated in Chen Hao's rebellion, he was put to death; his sons were sent to Fengyang; the line was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Bing, King Daoshun's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Hongzhi year 12; in Zhengde year 15, implicated in Chen Hao's rebellion, he was executed, his sons were sent to Fengyang, and the line was abolished.

cells.content: 樂安 昭定王奠壘，惠庶三子，景泰二年以鎮國將軍加封。弘治元年薨。

translations.literal: Le'an: King Zhaoding Dian Lei, the third son by a concubine of King Hui, in the second year of Jingtai received an additional enfeoffment as Defender of the State General. He died in the first year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Le'an — King Zhaoding (Dian Lei), King Hui's third son by a concubine, was additionally enfeoffed from Defender of the State General rank in Jingtai year 2 and died in Hongzhi 1.

cells.content: 覲鑉，昭定庶一子，成化四年封鎮國將軍。十七年卒。以子宸湔襲郡封，追封王，諡溫隱。

translations.literal: Guan, the first son by a concubine of King Zhaoding, was enfeoffed as Defender of the State General in the fourth year of Chenghua. He died in the seventeenth year. His son Chen Jian succeeded to the commandery enfeoffment; he was posthumously enfeoffed as king with the posthumous title Wenyin.

translations.literal: King Jingzhuang Chen Jian, the first son by the principal wife of King Wenyin, succeeded in the fourth year of Hongzhi and died in the twenty-first year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: King Jingzhuang (Chen Jian), King Wenyin's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Hongzhi year 4 and died in Jiajing year 21.

cells.content: 端簡王拱欏，靖莊嫡一子，嘉靖二十四年襲封。三十八年薨。

translations.literal: King Duanjian Gong, the first son by the principal wife of King Jingzhuang, succeeded in the twenty-fourth year of Jiajing and died in the thirty-eighth year.
translations.idiomatic: King Duanjian (Gong ), King Jingzhuang's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Jiajing year 24 and died in year 38.

translations.literal: Prince Duo Huang, the first son by the principal wife of King Duanjian, succeeded in the fortieth year of Jiajing and died sometime during the Wanli reign.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Duo (Huang), King Duanjian's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Jiajing year 40 and died during the Wanli reign.

translations.literal: Prince Mou 𩔇, the first son by a concubine of Prince Duo Huang, was enfeoffed as eldest son in the forty-third year of Wanli. He succeeded in the second year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mou (𩔇), Prince Duo Huang's first son by a concubine, was made eldest son in Wanli year 43 and inherited in Tianqi year 2.

cells.content: 石城 恭靖王奠堵，惠庶四子，景泰二年以鎮國將軍加封。成化二十二年薨。

translations.literal: Shicheng: King Gongjing Dian Du, the fourth son by a concubine of King Hui, in the second year of Jingtai received an additional enfeoffment as Defender of the State General. He died in the twenty-second year of Chenghua.

translations.literal: Guan Hao, the first son by a concubine of King Gongjing, was first enfeoffed as Defender of the State General. He died in the twenty-first year of Chenghua. His son Chen Fu succeeded to the enfeoffment; he was posthumously enfeoffed as king with the posthumous title Duanyin.

cells.content: 安恪王宸浮，端隱嫡一子，弘治二年襲封。十二年革爵。嘉靖二十四年奏復冠帶。二十七年卒。無子，除。

translations.literal: King Anke Chen Fu, the first son by the principal wife of King Duanyin, succeeded in the second year of Hongzhi. In the twelfth year his title was stripped. In the twenty-fourth year of Jiajing he memorialized and had his cap and belt restored. He died in the twenty-seventh year. He had no sons; the line was abolished.

translations.literal: Zhongling: Guan Zhui, the third son by a concubine of Prince Jing, was enfeoffed in the ninth year of Chenghua. translations.idiomatic: King Kangyi (Duo ), King Zhaojing's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Wanli 1 and died in year 29.

cells.content: 岷 莊王楩，太祖庶十八子，洪武二十四年封。二十八年就藩雲南。建文元年削籍。永樂元年復封。洪熙元年遷武岡州。景泰元年薨。

translations.literal: Min: Prince Zhuang Fan, the eighteenth son by a concubine of Taizu, was enfeoffed in the twenty-fourth year of Hongwu. In the twenty-eighth year he went to his fief in Yunnan. In the first year of Jianwen his registry was struck. In the first year of Yongle he was re-enfeoffed. In the first year of Hongxi he was moved to Wugang Prefecture. He died in the first year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: Min princedom — Prince Zhuang (Fan), Taizu's eighteenth son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in Hongwu year 24, took up his fief in Yunnan in year 28, was struck from the registry in Jianwen 1, was re-enfeoffed in Yongle 1, was transferred to Wugang Prefecture in Hongxi 1, and died in Jingtai 1.

translations.idiomatic: King Xian (Ding Yao), King Kang's second son by a concubine, inherited in Jiajing year 34 and died.

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Xijing Gan Gui, the first son by a concubine of King Xian, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Nanchong. In the fifteenth year of Wanli he was changed to heir apparent enfeoffment. He died in the twentieth year.

translations.literal: Heir-apparent grandson Qi Qin, the first son by the principal wife of Heir Apparent Xijing, was enfeoffed as heir-apparent grandson in the twenty-eighth year of Wanli. He died in the forty-second year. Prince Qi 𫓐, the second son by the principal wife of Heir Apparent Xijing, was first enfeoffed as commandery prince. In the fourth year of Chongzhen he was advanced in enfeoffment. In the sixteenth year he was robbed and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Heir-apparent grandson Qi (Qin), Heir Apparent Xijing's eldest son by his principal consort, was made heir-apparent grandson in Wanli year 28 and died in year 42. Prince Qi (𫓐), Heir Apparent Xijing's second son by his principal consort, was first a commandery prince, was promoted in Chongzhen year 4, and was robbed and killed in year 16.

translations.literal: Prince Yin Hong, the first son by the principal wife of Qi Qin, during the Wanli reign was enfeoffed as heir-apparent great-grandson. He succeeded in the second year of Tianqi and died in the first year of Chongzhen. He had no sons; his uncle Qi 𫓐 was established [in the line].

translations.idiomatic: Prince Gan Wa, Prince Ding Zhu's eldest son by his principal consort, was made eldest son in Wanli year 2, soon inherited the title, and died.

cells.content: 企𨥷，幹蛙庶一子，萬曆二十年封長孫。四十二年卒。

translations.literal: Qi Jin, the first son by a concubine of Prince Gan Wa, was enfeoffed as eldest grandson in the twentieth year of Wanli. He died in the forty-second year.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Jin, Prince Gan Wa's first son by a concubine, was made eldest grandson in Wanli year 20 and died in year 42.

cells.content: 王禋泞，企𨥷嫡一子，萬曆四十五年封曾長孫，既而襲封。

translations.literal: Prince Yin Ning, the first son by the principal wife of Qi Jin, was enfeoffed as eldest great-grandson in the forty-fifth year of Wanli and soon afterward succeeded to the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yin Ning, Qi Jin's eldest son by his principal consort, was made eldest great-grandson in Wanli year 45 and soon inherited the title.

cells.content: 廣濟 王定㸁，康庶八子，嘉靖三十六年封。萬曆二十七年薨。

translations.literal: Guangji: Prince Ding Han, the eighth son by a concubine of King Kang, was enfeoffed in the thirty-sixth year of Jiajing. He died in the twenty-seventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Guangji — Prince Ding Han, King Kang's eighth son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in Jiajing year 36 and died in Wanli year 27.

cells.content: 幹腫，定㸁嫡一子，萬曆九年封長子。三十六年頒冊，未受命，卒。無子，除。

translations.literal: Gan Zhong, the first son by the principal wife of Prince Ding Han, was enfeoffed as eldest son in the ninth year of Wanli. In the thirty-sixth year the patent was issued, but he died before receiving investiture. He had no sons, and the line was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhong, Prince Ding Han's eldest son by his principal consort, was made eldest son in Wanli year 9. In year 36 the investiture patent was issued, but he died before receiving it without heirs; the line was abolished.

cells.content: 青林 王幹垣，憲庶三子，嘉靖四十五年封，本年薨。無子，除。

translations.literal: Qinglin: Prince Gan Yuan, the third son by a concubine of King Xian, was enfeoffed in the forty-fifth year of Jiajing and died that same year. He had no sons, and the line was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Qinglin — Prince Gan Yuan, King Xian's third son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in Jiajing year 45 and died the same year without heirs; the line was abolished.

cells.content: 常寧 王幹坤，憲庶四子，萬曆十五年封。四十五年薨。無子，除。

translations.literal: Changning: Prince Gan Kun, the fourth son by a concubine of King Xian, was enfeoffed in the fifteenth year of Wanli. He died in the forty-fifth year. He had no sons, and the line was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Changning — Prince Gan Kun, King Xian's fourth son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in Wanli year 15 and died in year 45 without heirs; the line was abolished.

cells.content: 谷 橞，太祖庶十九子，洪武二十四年封。二十八年就藩宣府。成祖既位，移長沙府。永樂十五年坐謀逆，削為庶人，自焚死，除。

translations.literal: Gu: Hui, the nineteenth son by a concubine of Taizu, was enfeoffed in the twenty-fourth year of Hongwu. In the twenty-eighth year he went to his fief at Xuanfu. After the Chengzu Emperor took the throne, he was moved to Changsha Prefecture. In the fifteenth year of Yongle he was convicted of treason, stripped to commoner status, died by self-immolation, and the line was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Gu princedom — Hui, Taizu's nineteenth son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in Hongwu year 24, took up his fief at Xuanfu in year 28, was transferred to Changsha Prefecture after the Chengzu Emperor acceded, and in Yongle year 15 was convicted of treason, stripped to commoner rank, died by self-immolation, and the line was abolished.

cells.content: 韓 憲王松，太祖庶二十子，洪武二十四年封，未就藩。永樂五年薨。

translations.literal: Han: Prince Xian Song, the twentieth son by a concubine of Taizu, was enfeoffed in the twenty-fourth year of Hongwu but never went to his fief. He died in the fifth year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: Han princedom — Prince Xian (Song), Taizu's twentieth son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in Hongwu year 24 but never took up his fief, and died in Yongle year 5.

cells.content: 恭王沖𤊨，憲嫡一子，永樂九年襲封。二十二年之藩平涼府。正統五年薨。

translations.literal: King Gong Chong Huo, the first son by the principal wife of Prince Xian, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the ninth year of Yongle. In the twenty-second year he established his fief at Pingliang Prefecture. He died in the fifth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: King Gong (Chong Huo), Prince Xian's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Yongle year 9, established his fief at Pingliang Prefecture in year 22, and died in Zhengtong year 5.

cells.content: 懷王範圯，恭庶一子，初封開城王，正統七年襲封。九年薨。無子。 靖王範𰉫，恭庶二子，初封西鄉王，正統十一年進封。景泰元年薨。

translations.literal: King Huai Fan Yi, the first son by a concubine of King Gong, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Kaicheng, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the seventh year of Zhengtong, and died in the ninth year. He had no sons. King Jing Fan Yang, the second son by a concubine of King Gong, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Xixiang and was advanced in enfeoffment in the eleventh year of Zhengtong. He died in the first year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: King Huai (Fan Yi), King Gong's first son by a concubine, was first Prince of Kaicheng, inherited in Zhengtong year 7, and died in year 9 without heirs. King Jing (Fan Yang), King Gong's second son by a concubine, was first Prince of Xixiang, was promoted to the main line in Zhengtong year 11, and died in Jingtai 1.

cells.content: 惠王徵釙，靖庶一子，初封高陵王，景泰元年襲封。成化五年薨。

translations.literal: King Hui Zheng Bo, the first son by a concubine of King Jing, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Gaoling, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the first year of Jingtai, and died in the fifth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: King Hui (Zheng Bo), King Jing's first son by a concubine, was first Prince of Gaoling, inherited in Jingtai 1, and died in Chenghua year 5.

cells.content: 悼王偕㳘，惠庶二子，初封廣安王，成化五年襲封。十年薨。無子。 康王偕灊，惠庶三子，初封彰化王，成化十二年進封。弘治十四年薨。

translations.literal: King Dao Xie Yong, the second son by a concubine of King Hui, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Guang'an, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the fifth year of Chenghua, and died in the tenth year. He had no sons. King Kang Xie Qian, the third son by a concubine of King Hui, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Zhanghua and was advanced in enfeoffment in the twelfth year of Chenghua. He died in the fourteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: King Dao (Xie Yong), King Hui's second son by a concubine, was first Prince of Guang'an, inherited in Chenghua year 5, and died in year 10 without heirs. King Kang (Xie Qian), King Hui's third son by a concubine, was first Prince of Zhanghua, was promoted in Chenghua year 12, and died in Hongzhi year 14.

cells.content: 昭王旭櫏，康嫡一子，初封渭源王，弘治十七年襲封。嘉靖十三年薨。

translations.literal: King Zhao Xu Hui, the first son by the principal wife of King Kang, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Weiyuan, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the seventeenth year of Hongzhi, and died in the thirteenth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao (Xu Hui), King Kang's eldest son by his principal consort, was first Prince of Weiyuan, inherited in Hongzhi year 17, and died in Jiajing year 13.

cells.content: 定王融燧，昭嫡二子，嘉靖十五年襲封。四十四年薨。

translations.literal: King Ding Rong Sui, the second son by the principal wife of King Zhao, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the fifteenth year of Jiajing. He died in the forty-fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: King Ding (Rong Sui), King Zhao's second son by his principal consort, inherited in Jiajing year 15 and died in year 44.

cells.content: 謨㙉，定嫡一子，嘉靖十八年封世子。四十年薨。諡悼恭。後子朗錡襲封，追封王，改諡曰安。

translations.literal: Mo Jie, the first son by the principal wife of King Ding, was enfeoffed as heir apparent in the eighteenth year of Jiajing. He died in the fortieth year, with the posthumous title Daogong. Later his son Lang Qi succeeded to the enfeoffment; he was posthumously enfeoffed as king, and the posthumous title was changed to An.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Jie, King Ding's eldest son by his principal consort, was made heir apparent in Jiajing year 18 and died in year 40 with the posthumous epithet Daogong. His son Lang Qi later inherited the title; Mo Jie was posthumously enfeoffed as king, and his epithet was changed to An.

cells.content: 端王朗錡，安嫡二子，嘉靖四十五年以鎮國將軍改封世孫。隆慶三年襲封。萬曆三十四年薨。

translations.literal: King Duan Lang Qi, the second son by the principal wife of King An, was reassigned from Defender of the State General to heir-apparent grandson in the forty-fifth year of Jiajing. He succeeded to the enfeoffment in the third year of Longqing. He died in the thirty-fourth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: King Duan (Lang Qi), King An's second son by his principal consort, was transferred from Defender of the State General to heir-apparent grandson in Jiajing year 45, inherited in Longqing year 3, and died in Wanli year 34.

cells.content: 敬安世子璟浤，端嫡一子，隆慶四年封世子。萬曆二十八年薨。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Jing Hong of Jing'an, the first son by the principal wife of King Duan, was enfeoffed as heir apparent in the fourth year of Longqing. He died in the twenty-eighth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Jing'an (Jing Hong), King Duan's eldest son by his principal consort, was made heir apparent in Longqing year 4 and died in Wanli year 28.

cells.content: 逵𣏌，敬安嫡一子，萬曆二十年封世孫。三十六年薨。

translations.literal: Kui Ji, the first son by the principal wife of King Jing'an, was enfeoffed as heir-apparent grandson in the twentieth year of Wanli. He died in the thirty-sixth year.
translations.idiomatic: Kui Ji, King Jing'an's eldest son by his principal consort, was made heir-apparent grandson in Wanli year 20 and died in year 36.

cells.content: 王亶塉，逵𣏌嫡一子，萬曆三十八年封世曾孫。三十九年襲封。崇禎十六年，賊陷平涼，被執。

translations.literal: Prince Dan Ji, the first son by the principal wife of Kui Ji, was enfeoffed as heir-apparent great-grandson in the thirty-eighth year of Wanli and succeeded to the enfeoffment in the thirty-ninth year. In the sixteenth year of Chongzhen, when bandits captured Pingliang, he was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dan Ji, Kui Ji's eldest son by his principal consort, was made heir-apparent great-grandson in Wanli year 38, inherited in year 39, and in Chongzhen year 16 was seized when rebels captured Pingliang.

cells.content: 襄陵 莊穆王沖秌，憲庶二子，永樂二年封。成化十三年薨。

translations.literal: Xiangling: King Zhuangmu Chong Qiu, the second son by a concubine of Prince Xian, was enfeoffed in the second year of Yongle. He died in the thirteenth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangling — King Zhuangmu (Chong Qiu), Prince Xian's second son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in Yongle year 2 and died in Chenghua year 13.

translations.literal: Hanyin: King Gonghui Zheng Di, the second son by a concubine of Prince Jing, was enfeoffed and afterward died. He had no sons. When the prince fell ill, his consort's father Zhou Xun plotted to bring in another man's child and install him; the boy grew up and received enfeoffment. In the fourteenth year of Chenghua the matter came to light; Xun was executed, and the men and women involved in the fraudulent enfeoffment were all ordered to commit suicide; the line was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Hanyin — King Gonghui Zheng Di, Prince Jing's second son by a concubine, was enfeoffed and died without sons. While the prince lay ill, his consort's father Zhou Xun schemed to substitute another man's child, who later received enfeoffment. In Chenghua year 14 the fraud was exposed; Xun was executed, and all parties to the false succession were ordered to take their own lives; the line was abolished.

cells.content: 勛𣴣，恭庶一子，初封福山王，嘉靖四年先薨。一子未名，卒。二子未封，卒。以從姪允栘嗣封，追封王，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: Xun Yuan, the first son by a concubine of King Gong, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Fushan and died first in the fourth year of Jiajing. One son died unnamed; two sons died without enfeoffment. His collateral nephew Yun Yi succeeded to the enfeoffment; he was posthumously enfeoffed as king, with the posthumous title Jing.

cells.content: 允榿，靖嫡二子，嘉靖六年管理府事。九年薨。無子。以再從弟允栘嗣封。追封王，諡曰懷。 憲王允栘，靖從弟，靈川王勛潪嫡一子，嘉靖五年襲封靈川王。九年，以懷王絕嗣，管理府事。十年嗣封。追諡其祖詮鉌為安王，父為惠王。二十八年薨。

translations.literal: Yun Qi, the second son by the principal wife of King Jing, administered the princely establishment from the sixth year of Jiajing. He died in the ninth year. He had no sons. His second cousin once removed Yun Yi succeeded to the enfeoffment; he was posthumously enfeoffed as king, with the posthumous title Huai. King Xian Yun Yi, a collateral cousin of King Jing and the first son by the principal wife of Prince Lingchuan Xun Zhen, succeeded as Prince of Lingchuan in the fifth year of Jiajing. In the ninth year, with King Huai's line extinct, he administered the princely establishment. He succeeded to the main line in the tenth year. He posthumously gave his grandfather Quan Hong the epithet An and his father the epithet Hui. He died in the twenty-eighth year.
translations.idiomatic: Yun Qi, King Jing's second son by his principal consort, administered the princely establishment from Jiajing year 6, died in year 9 without heirs, and was posthumously made king with the epithet Huai when his second cousin once removed Yun Yi inherited. King Xian Yun Yi, King Jing's collateral cousin and Prince Lingchuan Xun Zhen's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited as Prince of Lingchuan in Jiajing year 5; when King Huai's line ended in year 9 he administered the establishment, succeeded to the main line in year 10, posthumously honored his grandfather Quan Hong as King An and his father as King Hui, and died in year 28.

translations.literal: Yun Yang, the first son by the principal wife of King Kangxi, was enfeoffed as eldest son in the thirteenth year of Zhengde. He died in the ninth year of Jiajing. His son Tian Wei succeeded to the enfeoffment; he was posthumously enfeoffed as king, with the posthumous title Daohe.

translations.literal: King Xiansu Cheng Chi, the second son by the principal wife of King Kangyu, in the fifth year of Wanli was changed from Defender of the State General to eldest-son enfeoffment. He succeeded in the thirteenth year and died in the thirty-fifth year.

translations.literal: Xiao Suo, the first son by a concubine of King Xiansu, in the ninth year of Wanli was changed from Bulwark of the State General to eldest-grandson enfeoffment. In the fifteenth year, for a crime he was reduced to commoner status. Prince Xiao Suo, the second son by a concubine of King Xiansu, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the forty-third year of Wanli.

cells.content: 榮僖王詮鏴，莊簡嫡四子，初封鎮國將軍，成化十三年繼黎城莊惠王嗣。後以莊簡三子俱卒，奏准歸宗。弘治十年襲封。正德十年薨。

translations.literal: King Rongxi Quan Lin, the fourth son by the principal wife of King Zhuangjian, was first enfeoffed as Defender of the State General. In the thirteenth year of Chenghua he succeeded to the line of King Zhuanghui of Licheng. Later, because all three sons of King Zhuangjian had died, a memorial was approved for return to the main line. He succeeded to the enfeoffment in the tenth year of Hongzhi. He died in the tenth year of Zhengde.

cells.content: 安 惠王楹，太祖庶二十二子，洪武二十四年封。永樂六年就藩平涼府。十五年薨。無子，封除。

translations.literal: An: Prince Hui Ying, the twenty-second son by a concubine of Taizu, was enfeoffed in the twenty-fourth year of Hongwu. In the sixth year of Yongle he went to his fief at Pingliang Prefecture. He died in the fifteenth year. He had no sons; the enfeoffment was abolished.

cells.content: 靖王瓊烴，定嫡一子，永樂二十一年襲封。宣德元年薨。無子。 憲王瓊炟，定嫡二子，宣德三年襲封。成化十一年薨。

translations.literal: King Jing Qiong Yan, the first son by the principal wife of Prince Ding, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the twenty-first year of Yongle. He died in the first year of Xuande. He had no sons. King Xian Qiong Ta, the second son by the principal wife of Prince Ding, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the third year of Xuande. He died in the eleventh year of Chenghua.

cells.content: 莊王芝址，憲嫡二子，初封舞陽王，成化十三年襲封。二十一年薨。

translations.idiomatic: King Zhuang Zhi Zhi, King Xian's second son by his principal consort, was first Prince of Wuyang, inherited in Chenghua year 13, and died in year 21.

cells.content: 成王彌鍗，莊庶一子，初封潁昌王，成化二十三年襲封。嘉靖二年薨。二子俱殀，姪宇溫嗣。

translations.literal: King Cheng Mi Jin, the first son by a concubine of King Zhuang, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yingchang. He succeeded to the enfeoffment in the twenty-third year of Chenghua. He died in the second year of Jiajing. Both sons died in infancy; his nephew Yu Wen succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: King Cheng Mi Jin, King Zhuang's first son by a concubine, was first Prince of Yingchang, inherited in Chenghua year 23, and died in Jiajing year 2. Both sons died in infancy, and his nephew Yu Wen succeeded.

cells.content: 敬王宇溫，成親弟文城王彌鉗嫡一子，初封文城王，嘉靖四年進封。追諡其父為恭王。三十九年薨。

translations.literal: King Jing Yu Wen, the first son by the principal wife of Wencheng King Mi Qian, younger brother of King Cheng, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Wencheng. In the fourth year of Jiajing he was advanced to the main enfeoffment. He posthumously gave his father the epithet Gong. He died in the thirty-ninth year.
translations.idiomatic: King Jing Yu Wen, Wencheng King Mi Qian's eldest son by his principal consort and King Cheng's younger brother by the same father, was first Prince of Wencheng, was promoted to the main Tang line in Jiajing year 4, posthumously gave his father the epithet Gong, and died in Jiajing year 39.

translations.idiomatic: King Shun Zhou Bing, King Jing's second son by a concubine, inherited in Jiajing year 41 and died in year 43.

cells.content: 端王碩熿，順庶一子，隆慶三年封世子。五年襲封。崇禎五年薨。

translations.literal: King Duan Shuo Huang, the first son by a concubine of King Shun, was enfeoffed as heir apparent in the third year of Longqing. He succeeded to the enfeoffment in the fifth year. He died in the fifth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: King Duan Shuo Huang, King Shun's first son by a concubine, was made heir apparent in Longqing year 3, inherited in year 5, and died in Chongzhen year 5.

cells.content: 器墭，端庶一子，萬曆二十二年封世子。後以端王惑於嬖人，被囚遇毒薨。追封王，諡曰裕。

translations.literal: Qi Zeng, the first son by a concubine of King Duan, was enfeoffed as heir apparent in the twenty-second year of Wanli. Later, because King Duan was deluded by a favorite and had him imprisoned, he met death by poison. He was posthumously enfeoffed as king, with the posthumous title Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Zeng, King Duan's first son by a concubine, was made heir apparent in Wanli year 22. Later, because King Duan was deluded by a favorite and had him imprisoned, he died by poison. He was posthumously made king with the epithet Yu.

cells.content: 聿鍵，裕嫡一子，初從世子被囚。萬曆中封世孫。崇禎五年襲封。九年以勤王違制，降為庶人，發鳳陽高牆。十七年五月赦出。次年奔福州自立，僭號隆武。大清順治三年八月奔汀州。王師至，被執死。 聿𨮁，裕嫡二子。聿鍵立，封為唐王。大清順治三年十一月，福建平，立於廣州，僭號紹武。踰月，王師至，被執死。

translations.literal: Yu Jian, the first son by the principal wife of King Yu, was at first imprisoned along with the heir apparent. During the Wanli reign he was enfeoffed as the heir's heir. He succeeded to the enfeoffment in the fifth year of Chongzhen. In the ninth year, for aiding the throne in violation of regulations, he was reduced to commoner status and sent to the high-walled prison at Fengyang. In the fifth month of the seventeenth year he was pardoned and released. The next year he fled to Fuzhou and declared himself emperor with the reign title Longwu. In the eighth month of the third year of Shunzhi of the Great Qing he fled to Tingzhou. When the imperial army arrived, he was captured and executed. Yu Yi, the second son by the principal wife of King Yu. When Yu Jian established himself, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Tang. In the eleventh month of the third year of Shunzhi of the Great Qing, after Fujian was pacified, he established himself at Guangzhou with the reign title Shaowu. Within a month the imperial army arrived, and he was captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jian, King Yu's eldest son by his principal consort, was initially imprisoned with the heir apparent, was enfeoffed as heir's heir during the Wanli reign, inherited in Chongzhen year 5, and in year 9 was demoted to commoner rank for aiding the throne in violation of regulations and sent to the Fengyang high-walled prison. Pardoned in the fifth month of Chongzhen year 17, he fled to Fuzhou the next year and declared himself emperor under the reign title Longwu. In the eighth month of Qing Shunzhi year 3 he fled to Tingzhou; when the imperial army arrived he was captured and executed. Yu Yi, King Yu's second son by his principal consort, was enfeoffed as Prince of Tang when Yu Jian established himself. In the eleventh month of Qing Shunzhi year 3, after Fujian was pacified, he established himself at Guangzhou under the reign title Shaowu; within a month the imperial army arrived and he was captured and executed.

translations.literal: King Rongxi Yu Hu, the first son by the principal wife of King Xuanyi, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the twelfth year of Hongzhi. He died in the thirty-second year of Jiajing.

cells.content: 器垌，碩燦庶一子。萬曆四十二年查父碩燦以弟冒兄爵，照世次，降封輔國將軍。 器𧯼，碩燁庶四子。萬曆四十六年，器垌以父冒封革襲，器𧯼請嗣郡爵。例封奉國將軍，奉祀，除。

translations.literal: Qi Dong, the first son by a concubine of Prince Shuo Can. In the forty-second year of Wanli an investigation found that his father Shuo Can had usurped his elder brother's title; according to succession order, he was reduced to Bulwark of the State General. Qi Cong, the fourth son by a concubine of Shuo Ye. In the forty-sixth year of Wanli, because Qi Dong's father's fraudulent succession was revoked, Qi Cong petitioned to inherit the commandery title. By regulation he was enfeoffed as Supporter of the State General to maintain sacrifices; the line was abolished.

cells.content: 萬安 康懿王典櫍，敬庶二子，嘉靖七年封。以奉祀。隆慶四年薨。

translations.literal: Wan'an: King Kangyi Dian Chu, the second son by a concubine of King Jing, was enfeoffed in the seventh year of Jiajing to maintain sacrifices. He died in the fourth year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: Wan'an — King Kangyi Dian Chu, King Jing's second son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in Jiajing year 7 to maintain ancestral rites and died in Longqing year 4.

cells.content: 昭和王襃𰞒，康懿嫡一子，萬曆二年襲封。二十六年薨。

translations.literal: King Zhaohe Bao 𰞒, the first son by the principal wife of King Kangyi, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the second year of Wanli. He died in the twenty-sixth year.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhaohe Bao 𰞒, King Kangyi's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Wanli year 2 and died in year 26.

cells.content: 恭宣王珂佳，昭和嫡一子，萬曆二十一年封長子。二十九年襲封。以就府營福藩，別城永寧，尋薨。

translations.literal: King Gongxuan Ke Jia, the first son by the principal wife of King Zhaohe, was enfeoffed as eldest son in the twenty-first year of Wanli. He succeeded to the enfeoffment in the twenty-ninth year. Because the princely residence was being developed for the Fu princedom, a separate city Yongning was walled; he soon died.
translations.idiomatic: King Gongxuan Ke Jia, King Zhaohe's eldest son by his principal consort, was designated heir in Wanli year 21 and inherited in year 29; because the princely seat was being rebuilt for the Fu princedom, a separate walled city at Yongning was established, and he soon died.

cells.content: 王采𨮫，恭宣嫡一子，襲封。崇禎九年二月以盜熾，請加築永寧城。十四年，闖賊破城，遇害。

translations.literal: Prince Cai 𨮫, the first son by the principal wife of King Gongxuan, succeeded to the enfeoffment. In the second month of the ninth year of Chongzhen, because banditry was rampant, he petitioned to reinforce the walls of Yongning. In the fourteenth year the roving rebels breached the city and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cai 𨮫, King Gongxuan's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited the title; in the second month of Chongzhen year 9, with banditry raging, he petitioned to strengthen Yongning's walls, and in year 14 the roving rebels stormed the city and killed him.

cells.content: 安樂 襃㸅，典楧庶五子，嘉靖二十九年封。三十二年革爵。四十三年卒。無子，除。

translations.literal: Anle: Bao, the fifth son by a concubine of Dian Yang, was enfeoffed in the twenty-ninth year of Jiajing. In the thirty-second year his title was stripped. He died in the forty-third year. He had no sons; the line was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Anle — Bao, Dian Yang's fifth son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in Jiajing year 29, was stripped of his title in year 32, died in year 43 without heirs, and the line was abolished.

cells.content: 靖江 守謙，太祖嫡兄南昌王興隆子文正嫡一子，洪武三年封。九年就藩桂林府，尋廢為庶人。七年復爵，使居雲南還鳳陽，後召錮京師。二十五年卒。

translations.literal: Jingjiang: Shouqian, the first son by the principal wife of King Wenzheng, who was the son of Prince Nanchang Xinglong, Taizu's elder full brother, was enfeoffed in the third year of Hongwu. In the ninth year he went to his fief at Guilin Prefecture and was soon demoted to commoner status. In the seventh year his title was restored; he was sent to live in Yunnan and then returned to Fengyang, and later was summoned and imprisoned in the capital. He died in the twenty-fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjiang princedom — Shouqian, eldest son by the principal consort of King Wenzheng and grandson of Prince Nanchang Xinglong, Taizu's elder full brother, was enfeoffed in Hongwu year 3, took up his fief at Guilin Prefecture in year 9 but was soon stripped to commoner rank, had his title restored in year 7, was sent to live in Yunnan and then Fengyang, was later summoned and confined in the capital, and died in year 25.

cells.content: 附 悼僖王贊儀，守謙嫡一子，建文二年襲封。永樂元年就藩。六年薨。

translations.literal: Annex: King Daoxi Zan Yi, the first son by the principal wife of Shouqian, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the second year of Jianwen. In the first year of Yongle he went to his fief. He died in the sixth year.
translations.idiomatic: Annex — King Daoxi Zan Yi, Shouqian's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Jianwen year 2, took up his fief in Yongle 1, and died in year 6.

cells.content: 莊簡王佐敬，悼僖庶一子，永樂九年襲封。成化五年薨。

translations.literal: King Zhuangjian Zuo Jing, the first son by a concubine of King Daoxi, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the ninth year of Yongle. He died in the fifth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhuangjian Zuo Jing, King Daoxi's first son by a concubine, inherited in Yongle year 9 and died in Chenghua year 5.

cells.content: 相承，莊簡嫡一子，正統元年封長子。天順二年卒。以子規裕襲封。追封王，諡懷順。

translations.literal: Xiang Cheng, the first son by the principal wife of King Zhuangjian, was enfeoffed as eldest son in the first year of Zhengtong. He died in the second year of Tianshun. His son Gui Yu succeeded to the enfeoffment; he was posthumously enfeoffed as king, with the posthumous title Huaishun.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Cheng, King Zhuangjian's eldest son by his principal consort, was designated heir in Zhengtong 1 and died in Tianshun year 2; his son Gui Yu inherited the line, and Xiang Cheng was posthumously made king with the epithet Huaishun.

translations.literal: King Zhaohe Gui Yu, the first son by the principal wife of King Huaishun, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the seventh year of Chenghua. He died in the second year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhaohe Gui Yu, King Huaishun's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Chenghua year 7 and died in Hongzhi year 2.

cells.content: 端懿王約麒，昭和嫡一子，弘治三年襲封。正德十一年薨。

translations.literal: King Duanyi Yue Qi, the first son by the principal wife of King Zhaohe, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the third year of Hongzhi. He died in the eleventh year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: King Duanyi Yue Qi, King Zhaohe's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Hongzhi year 3 and died in Zhengde year 11.

cells.content: 安肅王經扶，端懿嫡一子，正德十三年襲封。嘉靖四年薨。

translations.literal: King Ansu Jing Fu, the first son by the principal wife of King Duanyi, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the thirteenth year of Zhengde. He died in the fourth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: King Ansu Jing Fu, King Duanyi's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Zhengde year 13 and died in Jiajing year 4.

cells.content: 恭惠王邦寧，安肅嫡一子，嘉靖六年襲封。隆慶六年薨。

translations.literal: King Gonghui Bang Ning, the first son by the principal wife of King Ansu, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the sixth year of Jiajing. He died in the sixth year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: King Gonghui Bang Ning, King Ansu's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Jiajing year 6 and died in Longqing year 6.

cells.content: 康僖王任昌，恭惠嫡一子，萬曆五年襲封。十年薨。 憲定王任晟，恭惠庶二子，萬曆二十年以輔國將軍進封。三十八年薨。長子履祥先卒。

translations.literal: King Kangxi Ren Chang, the first son by the principal wife of King Gonghui, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the fifth year of Wanli. He died in the tenth year. King Xianding Ren Sheng, the second son by a concubine of King Gonghui, in the twentieth year of Wanli was advanced to enfeoffment from Bulwark of the State General. He died in the thirty-eighth year. His eldest son Lu Xiang had died earlier.
translations.idiomatic: King Kangxi Ren Chang, King Gonghui's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Wanli year 5 and died in year 10. King Xianding Ren Sheng, King Gonghui's second son by a concubine, was promoted from Bulwark of the State General rank in Wanli year 20, died in year 38, and his eldest son Lu Xiang had predeceased him.

cells.content: 溫裕王履燾，康僖嫡一子，萬曆十三年襲封。二十年薨。無子。叔任晟立。 榮穆王履祐，憲定嫡二子，萬曆二十八年以奉國將軍改封長子。四十年襲封，薨。

translations.literal: King Wenyu Lu Tan, the first son by the principal wife of King Kangxi, succeeded to the enfeoffment in the thirteenth year of Wanli. He died in the twentieth year. He had no sons. His uncle Ren Sheng succeeded. King Rongmu Lu You, the second son by the principal wife of King Xianding, in the twenty-eighth year of Wanli was changed from Supporter of the State General to eldest-son enfeoffment. He succeeded to the enfeoffment in the fortieth year and died.
translations.idiomatic: King Wenyu Lu Tan, King Kangxi's eldest son by his principal consort, inherited in Wanli year 13 and died in year 20 without heirs; his uncle Ren Sheng succeeded. King Rongmu Lu You, King Xianding's second son by his principal consort, was redesignated heir from Supporter of the State General rank in Wanli year 28, inherited in year 40, and died.

cells.content: 王亨嘉，榮穆庶一子，萬曆四十三年封長子。崇禎中襲封。大清順治二年叛，稱監國，為福王總督丁魁楚、巡撫瞿式耜所殺。

translations.literal: Prince Heng Jia, the first son by a concubine of King Rongmu, was enfeoffed as eldest son in the forty-third year of Wanli. During the Chongzhen reign he succeeded to the enfeoffment. In the second year of Shunzhi under the Great Qing he rebelled, proclaimed himself regent, and was killed by Ding Kuitchu, supreme commander for the Prince of Fu, and Qu Shiji, provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Heng Jia, King Rongmu's first son by a concubine, was designated heir in Wanli year 43 and inherited during the Chongzhen reign; in the second year of Shunzhi under the Great Qing he rebelled, styled himself regent, and was killed by Ding Kuitchu, supreme commander for the Prince of Fu, and Qu Shiji, provincial governor.
